questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

A medical team provides vaccinations for children to prevent an outbreak of an infectious disease. Why would this be described as a positive externality?

options.A: Additional benefit might be gained as the disease no longer spreads.
options.B: Any kind of medical help will improve the condition of the children.
options.C: No action would be taken unless the medical team intervened.
options.D: The social benefits of vaccination are less than the social costs.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the cost and revenue curves for a firm. Which output level will enable a firm to achieve its objective of maximising its revenue? MC price AC P P P P MR

options.D: = AR O A B C D quantity

questions.questionText: Oligopoly firms seek to maximise profits. How will this affect the pricing behaviour of oligopoly firms involved in a non-collusive market?

options.A: A price is fixed for the product that never changes throughout its life cycle.
options.B: Firms will agree on the level of advertising costs for a new product.
options.C: If one firm raises its price, other firms will maintain their original price to increase their market share.
options.D: If one firm lowers its price, other firms will increase their price.

questions.questionText: An economic activity definitely creates a net social benefit when the value of social benefit minus

options.A: private benefit is zero.
options.B: private benefit is negative.
options.C: social cost is positive.
options.D: social cost is negative.

questions.questionText: Which assumption is essential for a market to be contestable?

options.A: The market is supplied by a large number of firms.
options.B: Firms are free to enter and leave the market.
options.C: Firms cannot earn abnormal profits in the short run.
options.D: Firms produce differentiated goods.

questions.questionText: A firm that raises capital through a share issue has to satisfy both shareholders’ expectations and management aims. The management aims to produce at a non-profit maximum output. Which strategy would necessarily prevent this aim?

options.A: fixing output where MC = MR in the long run
options.B: operating price discrimination to maximise revenue
options.C: rewarding shareholders more than returns to innovation
options.D: separating ownership and control of the firm

questions.questionText: A major UK chemical firm was bought by its rival, a Dutch chemical firm. What definitely occurred when the Dutch firm bought the UK firm?

options.A: a partnership
options.B: economies of scale
options.C: horizontal integration
options.D: increased profits

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct for a firm classed as a natural monopoly?

options.A: It will always operate in the public sector and earn normal profits.
options.B: It will have high barriers to entry and be the dominant producer.
options.C: It will easily benefit from external economies of scale.
options.D: It will have higher average costs than a monopolistically competitive firm.

questions.questionText: The government can use policies to try and reduce the environmental damage caused by the amount of rubbish (garbage) created by firms and households. Which policy to reduce rubbish is most likely to lead to government failure?

options.A: an incentive payment for firms who reduce the levels of rubbish
options.B: a tax on the amount of rubbish a firm or household creates
options.C: an advertising campaign about the problems created by rubbish
options.D: government grants to firms researching how to safely dispose of rubbish

questions.questionText: What would supporters of a nationalised public transport service expect to be the most likely outcome from the privatisation of train and bus services?

options.A: fewer destinations served by trains and buses
options.B: lower fares
options.C: more frequent services to all destinations
options.D: more people employed in public transport services

questions.questionText: What will cause a household to be caught in the poverty trap?

options.A: A household earns less than the international poverty line of $2.15 per person per day.
options.B: A household spends more than it earns in a month.
options.C: A household’s earnings rise at a lower rate than the rise in inflation.
options.D: An extra dollar earnt by a household causes a greater loss in government benefit payments.

questions.questionText: What will cause an outward shift in the demand for labour curve?

options.A: a decrease in the top rate of income tax
options.B: an increase in the demand for the final product
options.C: an increase in subsidies to firms
options.D: an increase in the size of the working population

A world financial crisis was partly linked to the actions of commercial banks. Which actions of the commercial banks could have led to the financial crisis?

options.A: being subject to tight controls by the central bank over credit creation
options.B: holding reserves above the reserve ratio agreed with the central bank
options.C: taking excessive risks by demanding insufficient security from borrowers
options.D: widening the gap in favour of a bank’s assets over liabilities

questions.questionText: What is most likely to result from a decrease in the natural rate of unemployment?

options.A: a decrease in government expenditure on goods and services
options.B: a decrease in the level of government payments to the unemployed
options.C: a decrease in trade union membership
options.D: a decrease in interest rates

questions.questionText: The table gives the percentage (%) rates of youth unemployment and total unemployment in France and the UK in 2001 and 2005. France UK youth total youth total unemployment unemployment unemployment unemployment (%) (%) (%) (%) 2001 19.2 8.7 12.0 5.2 2005 22.1 10.1 12.5 4.8 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: France and the UK experienced the same trends in unemployment.
options.B: France had a higher number of unemployed people than the UK.
options.C: The UK used a different definition of unemployment from France.
options.D: The UK was more successful than France in controlling unemployment.

questions.questionText: What is a necessary assumption of the Keynesian multiplier model?

options.A: increasing average propensity to save
options.B: flexible costs and prices
options.C: full employment of resources
options.D: open economies

An economy has a sudden increase in inflation caused by a large rise in energy prices. It also enters a recession with rising unemployment.

options.A: direct taxation
options.B: government spending
options.C: indirect taxation
options.D: interest rate

questions.questionText: What is not a threat to globalisation?

options.A: rising fear of losing jobs to immigrant workers
options.B: rising political tensions among major economies of the world
options.C: stronger trade unions in industries producing substitutes of imports
options.D: withdrawal of government support for inefficient industries

questions.questionText: Singapore has one of the highest population densities in the world. It discourages car use through a high tax on second cars. Which additional policy would help to relieve road congestion in the short run?

options.A: limiting the total number of car licences issued
options.B: encouraging restrictions on the size of families
options.C: improving infrastructure by building new roads
options.D: replacing diesel cars by electric cars

questions.questionText: What is not an example of an expenditure-reducing policy?

options.A: a decrease in government spending
options.B: a depreciation of the exchange rate
options.C: an increase in direct taxes
options.D: an increase in interest rates

questions.questionText: What does the J-curve effect show?

options.A: A successful currency depreciation requires the sum of the import and export elasticities of demand to be greater than 1.
options.B: After a currency devaluation, the current account is likely to get worse before it gets better.
options.C: In the short run, the demand for imports and exports tends to be price elastic.
options.D: The value of the terms of trade will affect the success of a currency’s devaluation.

questions.questionText: What is the most likely consequence of an increase in the number of multinational companies?

options.A: a decrease in advancements in technology
options.B: a decrease in foreign direct investment
options.C: an increase in exports
options.D: an increase in unemployment

questions.questionText: The table shows the GDP and population of four countries. Which country is most likely to have the lowest standard of living? GDP population country US$ billion million

options.A: Bangladesh 206.7 153.5
options.C: Nigeria 292.7 138.3
options.D: South Africa 467.1 43.8

questions.questionText: What will increase the size of a country’s optimum population?

options.A: a rise in the birth rate
options.B: a lowering of the age of retirement
options.C: a rise in the stock of capital available in the country
options.D: a decrease in the productivity of the country’s industries
